data.name: Google Picks Blue Origin to Launch Orbital AI Satellites for Project Suncatcher
data.summary: Google has selected Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to launch satellites for Project Suncatcher, aiming to run AI systems in orbit using solar power, with a first mission set for early 2029 on the New Glenn rocket. Each satellite packs Tensor Processing Units equal to a full data-center rack and will orbit in constant sunlight. A prototype already succeeded in October, generating a haiku poem in space, as the company tackles AI's growing demands for electricity and cooling on Earth. The deal marks a key step for Blue Origin's rocket after setbacks and highlights space as a potential solution for AI infrastructure.

data.summary: Primus Labs offers a pluggable privacy layer using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) and zkTLS, allowing encrypted data to stay on existing blockchains for computations while keeping numbers hidden by default. Practical examples include verifying stablecoin reserves on exchanges and proving Web3 membership without screenshots, with claims of fast 90-millisecond transfers and over $72 million in verified proof-of-reserves TVL.
